source.shell: frontend/index.html (favicon only; the direction contract is no longer embedded in the document)
source.direction: .impeccable/surfaces/frontend-src-app-tsx.md (the amended direction contract: El Mosaico de Días)

ink-deep.displayName: Ink Deep (the ink under the hand)

display.purpose: The house name in the letterhead. 1.32rem / 900 / -0.02em, uppercase, line-height 1.

figure.purpose: The closing total ("Te queda"): clamp(1.06rem, 4.6vw, 1.72rem) Chivo Mono, tabular. The largest number on the sheet, and the only one that turns red when the month closes negative.

subtotal.purpose: The income and expense figures beside it on the month's band: clamp(0.94rem, 3.4vw, 1.22rem) Chivo Mono, tabular.

ticket-amount.purpose: A facturita's amount on its header line and the cap field: 1.02rem Chivo Mono, tabular, pushed to the right edge by margin-left: auto.

heading.purpose: The .sect h2 of every band: 0.74rem / 900 / 0.16em, uppercase, on the baseline of its 1px rule.

body.purpose: Reading copy, notes, hints and notices: 16px Libre Franklin at 1.45, measure capped at 66-74ch.

label.purpose: Field labels, plate lettering and .tag: 0.66rem / 700 / 0.14em, uppercase.

mono-micro.purpose: The document number Nº YYYY-MM, a facturita's correlative Nº and its date, the day count, the page folio and the pager state: 0.68-0.76rem Chivo Mono. A facturita's correlative Nº and its date sit at the top of that range (0.76rem, raised from 0.68rem) and the ticket's wallet line and note are 0.82rem (≈13.1px), so the smallest reading copy on a facturita clears the 13px floor the printed charts already set.

shadows.name: sheet-rest
shadows.purpose: The sheet lying on the light honey board at rest (below 720px, where it is not tilted): a warm 1px hairline at the top edge plus one offset, soft, negatively-spread, warm ground shadow. Warm because it is cast on wood, not grey, and it is what holds the paper's silhouette against the board, since the sheet's hairline edge measures under the 3:1 a rim would need.

shadows.name: sheet-pinned
shadows.purpose: The same sheet read as pinned: from 720px up the sheet carries a rotate(-0.3deg) tilt (The Three Pinned Breaks), and its warm contact shadow tightens to a slightly firmer 0.16 hairline over a closer, marginally darker ground so it reads as lying pinned to the board, not floating. Desktop-only, because the transform would make the fixed action plate resolve against the sheet below 720px.

shadows.name: facturita-tear
shadows.purpose: The one shadow each torn facturita's <li> carries, as a filter and never a box-shadow (which the tear's mask clips). It follows the torn silhouette, and because the tickets rest on the sheet and not on the board it is the only thing that makes the tear legible.

shadows.name: month-arrow
shadows.purpose: The short paper shadow under each 46px month arrow circle, dropping to 0 1px 2px -1px while pressed. One of the three pinned breaks of the document's squareness (The Three Pinned Breaks).

shadows.name: window-over
shadows.purpose: A window thrown over the sheet. Never applied to a band, a field or a facturita.

shadows.name: plate-float
shadows.purpose: The action plate once it leaves the flow and floats over the sheet on a phone (below 720px, .membrete .plate position: fixed). Its only drop shadow; in the flow the plate carries just its inset edge.

shadows.name: double-rule
shadows.purpose: Draws the second line of the double rule under the 3px ink border of .membrete, the month's band .subtotals and .wtitle. It is a rule, not depth.

shadows.name: plate-edge
shadows.purpose: The printed lower edge of the action plate at rest.

shadows.name: plate-press
shadows.purpose: The plate's edge once the stamp goes down (:active), together with translateY(1px).

shadows.name: scrim
shadows.purpose: A flat ink wash behind a window. No backdrop-filter, no blur: the scrim dims the desk, it never frosts it.

motion.name: ink-dry
motion.purpose: The first authored moment: the month's figures re-print in place (opacity 0.35 -> 1). Replayed by remounting the value spans with App's repaintKey after a save or a month change (KpiSummary, .repaint).

motion.name: ink-set
motion.purpose: The second authored moment: the facturita just written is ringed once by an inset 2px stamp ring (inset 0 0 0 2px rgba(178, 58, 32, 0.5) -> transparent) as the ink sets (.tickets .flash .fact, .pin-row .flash .fact).

motion.name: plate-state
motion.purpose: Hover deepens the stamp fill; pressing moves the plate down 1px and flips its inset edge.

motion.name: skip-link-slide
motion.purpose: The skip link slides into the top-left corner on focus (.skip-link, top: -100px -> 14px).

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce nothing moves and every state stays readable.

breakpoints.name: board-narrow
breakpoints.purpose: The phone's board band is only ~18px wide, and the wide desktop grain (a hairline at alpha 0.06 on a 3px period) reads there as a flat colour band, not as wood: html carries a second authored background set — knots of ~9px at x 2%/97.5%, a plank joint every 54px, three grain periods of 3px/5px/4px at alphas 0.16/0.11/0.09, and a 180° tonal ramp that runs down the band instead of across it. The same board drawn for the room it has; the cost is two rule sets to keep in step (The Authored-Board Rule).

breakpoints.name: desk
breakpoints.purpose: The sheet lifts off the board: width min(1400px, 100% - 120px), 30px auto margins and 34px 40px 46px padding, guaranteeing at least 60px of board on each side. Below it the sheet is width min(1400px, 100% - 36px) with margin: 18px auto — an 18px cravat of board all around it, the same paper over the same board as on the desktop, with the controls and the pieces at their usual sizes — and that ~18px band is the board redrawn at the narrow scale (see the board-narrow breakpoint).

breakpoints.name: columns
breakpoints.purpose: The .mosaic of day blocks, .cols (donut + bars), .two (window form rows) and .jar-meta (reassignment selects) become two columns.

breakpoints.name: columns-wide
breakpoints.purpose: The .mosaic of day blocks goes to three columns; the desktop sheet carries ~395px day blocks.

breakpoints.name: phone
breakpoints.purpose: Below this the letterhead's action plate leaves the flow (position: fixed, 16px from the right and bottom edges, z-index: 30) with the body reserving 104px of foot, and the pagination's buttons stack into a column so they never sit under the floating plate. The sheet's pin is redrawn here too: .sheet-pin svg drops from 42x31.5px to 26x19.5px, because the phone's board edge is only 18px and the desktop size pushed the head off the top of the screen.

breakpoints.name: pointer-coarse
breakpoints.purpose: Raises every control below the comfortable minimum to 44px: .linkb, .fact-acts .linkb, .pinb, .iconb (width included), .pbtn, .row .capfield and .monthjump input[type=month]. Declared last in index.css on purpose: at equal specificity these only win by order, and higher up they stay inert.

breakpoints.name: jar-figures
breakpoints.purpose: A jar's three figures (.jar-figs: Objetivo / Gastado / Restante) keep their three-column grid (repeat(3, minmax(0, 1fr))) from 560px up. Below 560px they collapse to one column and each cell becomes a row — label left, figure right, a 1px --color-rule hairline between — because at 390px a three-column grid leaves each figure only ~87px while a long mono amount needs 105–112px and spilled into its neighbour (measured).

browserSurfaces.name: selection
browserSurfaces.purpose: Selected text is ink struck by the stamp.

browserSurfaces.name: caret
browserSurfaces.purpose: The caret is the pen in the document's ink.

browserSurfaces.name: scrollbars
browserSurfaces.value: scrollbar-width: thin; scrollbar-color: var(--color-rule-strong) transparent; ::-webkit-scrollbar 10px, thumb 2px transparent border with background-clip: content-box
browserSurfaces.purpose: The scrollbars of the bars scroller and a window body belong to the palette.

browserSurfaces.name: focus-ring
browserSurfaces.purpose: One visible ring everywhere, in the stamp's red; the cap field and the bars scroller restate it.

browserSurfaces.name: print
browserSurfaces.value: @media print hides .monthnav, .pager, .filters, .fact-acts, .skip-link, .sheet-pin, .plate, .action-stamp; the sheet loses its shadow, its border, its max-width and its tilt (transform: none)
browserSurfaces.purpose: A real document also leaves by printer; the drawn pin is decoration and the -0.3deg tilt is a screen gesture, so both are dropped on paper.

fonts.purpose: The document face: house name, section heads, labels, body copy.
The measuring face at reading weight (pager ranges, chart labels).
Every amount, rate, date, count and correlative number.

accessibility.liveRegion: frontend/src/components/LiveRegion.tsx - the app's only role="status" region; announcements replace each other. The visible Notice is deliberately not a live region.

contrast.method: Ratios computed from the @theme token values, compositing rgba over the sheet's paper ground. A browser walk of every text node (verify.cjs) was re-run for the reconciliation pass: 0 failures over 339 text nodes at 1440 and 390, counting ancestor opacity. The two inkDim figures on paper are the owner's re-measured values after the secondary-ink step (the tokens' own comments in index.css state 8,8:1 and 5,7:1); the Copy Paper variants below are the same composition arithmetic run over #f2f3f0 against the token alphas.

constraints: Touch targets 42-46px at rest (.plate/.field/.seg 46px, .pbtn/.iconb 42px, .pinb/.linkb 34px, .skip-link 44px) with a 44px floor on a coarse pointer.
Every control has an associated label; the gasto/ingreso, USD/VES and import groups are role=radiogroup with an aria-label.
Form errors use aria-invalid + aria-describedby and focus moves to the first field with an error; no role=alert per field.

Each movement detail line validates inline (aria-invalid + aria-describedby to its own error) and every control names its row in its aria-label; a line's price field carries a visible currency label ("Precio (Bs)" / "Precio ($)") while its accessible name stays "Precio de la línea N"; the jars' role=progressbar and its aria-valuetext are untouched.
No window.confirm anywhere: every interruption is the one Window primitive with focus moved in, trapped, restored, Escape to close and body scroll locked.
The board's search is a native input[type=search]; each facturita is an article and each day block a list item, so the mosaic keeps list semantics.

superseded: docs/architecture.md still documents the retired teal system (single hue 188, paletteFor, dark mode). docs/** is frozen by the project's ownership contract, so it was not edited; DESIGN.md supersedes it for visual decisions.

.impeccable/NEW-WORLD-SPEC.md and .impeccable/build-packet.md describe the previous chalk-board world ("La pizarra de la tasa", board/chalk/wood tokens, the #paint-rough filter). index.css no longer carries any of those tokens or classes; the contract also no longer ships inside frontend/index.html.

The incumbent DESIGN.md described the month as one invoice with a numbered ledger table (.book, .book .ln, .book .desc, .book .acts, .table-scroll) and a .leader dot leader. That surface was replaced by the board of facturitas (El Mosaico de Días); every one of those rules is retired and removed.

components.name: Action Plate
components.description: The single saturated fill on the sheet: one stamp-red plate per flow — Anotar movimiento in the letterhead, Agregar movimiento / Guardar cambios in the movement window, Reemplazar todo in the import window, and the destructive confirm. The wallet window's confirm is the ink plate, not this one.

components.name: Page Button
components.description: The document's secondary control: pager steps, Mes actual, Exportar, Importar, Reintentar, Nueva cartera and the window cancel actions.

components.css: .ds-pbtn { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; min-height: 42px; padding: 9px 14px; border: 1px solid var(--color-control); border-radius: 0; background: var(--color-paper); color: var(--color-ink); font-family: var(--font-sans); font-size: 0.72rem; font-weight: 700; letter-spacing: 0.1em; text-transform: uppercase; cursor: pointer; transition: background-color 120ms ease, border-color 120ms ease; } .ds-pbtn:hover:not(:disabled) { border-color: var(--color-ink); background: var(--color-paper-2); } .ds-pbtn:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--color-danger); outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-pbtn:disabled { color: var(--color-dim-2); cursor: not-allowed; }

components.name: Month Arrow
components.description: The month's step control: a 46px paper circle with a 1px Control Line border, flanking the centred month name in .monthnav-main. One of the three pinned breaks of the document's squareness (The Three Pinned Breaks), with a short paper shadow that drops while pressed.

components.css: .ds-mnav { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; width: 46px; height: 46px; padding: 0; border: 1px solid var(--color-control); border-radius: 50%; background: var(--color-paper); color: var(--color-ink); cursor: pointer; box-shadow: 0 3px 5px -2px rgba(58, 36, 10, 0.38); transition: background-color 120ms ease, transform 60ms ease, box-shadow 120ms ease; } .ds-mnav:hover { background: var(--color-paper-2); border-color: var(--color-ink); } .ds-mnav:active { transform: translateY(1px); box-shadow: 0 1px 2px -1px rgba(58, 36, 10, 0.38); } .ds-mnav:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--color-danger); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Ink Plate
components.description: The page-button frame filled with print ink: the confirm action inside the wallet window (Crear cartera / Guardar cambios). Hover drops ground and border to Ink Deep — the token's only use. The red plate stays reserved for the document's action and for the destructive confirm.
components.html: <button class="ds-pbtn-primary" type="button">GUARDAR CAMBIOS</button>
components.css: .ds-pbtn-primary { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; min-height: 42px; padding: 9px 14px; border: 1px solid var(--color-ink); border-radius: 0; background: var(--color-ink); color: var(--color-paper); font-family: var(--font-sans); font-size: 0.72rem; font-weight: 700; letter-spacing: 0.1em; text-transform: uppercase; cursor: pointer; transition: background-color 120ms ease, border-color 120ms ease; } .ds-pbtn-primary:hover:not(:disabled) { background: var(--color-ink-deep); border-color: var(--color-ink-deep); } .ds-pbtn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--color-danger); outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-pbtn-primary:disabled { color: var(--color-dim-2); cursor: not-allowed; }

components.name: Segmented Control
components.description: A 1px-bordered rectangle divided by 1px separators; the chosen option turns ink with paper lettering. Used for gasto/ingreso, USD/VES and the import modes (role=radiogroup, aria-checked). A segment is disabled for real only while it is not offered — the import modes while an import is in flight — with a Copy Paper ground, Ink Dim 2 lettering and cursor: not-allowed; the chosen-segment rule is declared after it, so the checked segment keeps its ink. The currency control is no longer one of those: with detail lines on screen both USD and VES stay selectable, and nothing forces USD.
components.css: .ds-seg { display: inline-flex; border: 1px solid var(--color-control); border-radius: 0; } .ds-seg-btn { min-height: 46px; padding: 10px 16px; border: 0; border-right: 1px solid var(--color-control); background: var(--color-paper); color: var(--color-dim); font-family: var(--font-sans); font-size: 0.74rem; font-weight: 700; letter-spacing: 0.1em; text-transform: uppercase; cursor: pointer; transition: background-color 120ms ease, color 120ms ease; } .ds-seg-btn:last-child { border-right: 0; } .ds-seg-btn:disabled { background: var(--color-paper-2); color: var(--color-dim-2); cursor: not-allowed; } .ds-seg-btn[aria-checked="true"] { background: var(--color-ink); color: var(--color-paper); } .ds-seg-btn:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--color-danger); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Text Field
components.description: The document's casillero: paper ground, 1px Control Line border, square corners, 46px tall. Focus and invalid states are the stamp's red. The board's search is the same casillero as a native input[type=search].
components.css: .ds-field { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 5px; min-width: 0; } .ds-field-label { font-family: var(--font-sans); font-size: 0.66rem; font-weight: 700; letter-spacing: 0.14em; text-transform: uppercase; color: var(--color-dim); } .ds-input { width: 100%; min-height: 46px; padding: 10px 12px; border: 1px solid var(--color-control); border-radius: 0; background: var(--color-paper); color: var(--color-ink); font-family: var(--font-sans); font-size: 0.92rem; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; } .ds-input::placeholder { color: var(--color-dim-2); } .ds-input:focus-visible { border-color: var(--color-danger); outline: 2px solid var(--color-danger); outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-input[aria-invalid="true"] { border-color: var(--color-danger); border-width: 2px; } .ds-input:disabled { background: var(--color-paper-2); color: var(--color-dim-2); }

components.name: Select
components.description: appearance: none with the chevron drawn in CSS (two 5px ink wedges); option is forced onto an opaque paper ground so the native popup never goes light under ink lettering.

components.description: The ruled band that reports an outcome on the sheet or inside a window: Copy Paper ground closed above by a 2px ink rule, never outlined down one side. components.name: Facturita
components.description: The month's atom: one little torn piece of paper per record. Square and printed above, torn along the bottom by an authored SVG mask ('--tear', a 320x12 path repeated at mask-size 320px 12px); each ticket's <li> carries one filter: drop-shadow (a filter, because the mask clips a box-shadow) and that shadow is the only thing that makes the tear legible, since the paper rests on the sheet and not on the board. Header line: correlative Nº (aria-hidden, 0.76rem), date (0.76rem), amount pushed right (the USD total, in full ink with its +/-); then the tag + category, the wallet and the note (0.82rem each, ≈13.1px; the ticket's two smallest roles each rose one step — 0.68→0.76rem for the correlative Nº and the date, 0.76→0.82rem for the wallet line and the note — so its smallest reading copy clears the 13px floor the printed charts already set), and the ballpoint .pen detail for a bolívar entry; below a 1px dashed --color-rule divider sit the alfiler and the .linkb actions. When the movement carries detail lines, a ul.fact-items opens between the body and the actions, above a 1px dashed --color-rule rule: one li.fact-item per line, its description (.fact-item-desc, Ink Dim) left and its price (.fact-item-amt, mono, tabular, nowrap) right, both in the movement's entry currency — a VES movement's lines render in bolívares (formatBss) while the header keeps the USD total; the breakdown never repeats the total.

components.name: Sheet Pin
components.description: The sheet read as pinned to the board: the pin is now its own engraved drawing (frontend/src/components/SheetPin.tsx, mounted as .sheet-pin), no longer a 26px inline PinIcon. A 40x30 viewBox drawn at 42x31.5px and at 26x19.5px below 719px: a head whose radial gradient runs from 0.4 to 1.0 of ink opacity — the same wide "engraved" opacity family the printed charts use, because a narrow range read as a flat black shape — an unprinted highlight on the dome (.sheet-pin-gleam, filled with --color-paper), the head's rim as a darker band (0.68), a collar (0.78) and the needle's entry into the paper (0.9), over a soft radial penumbra (0.34 / 0.14 / 0) for the cast shadow, which read as a flat base before. Its gradient stops take their colour from the token (.sheet-pin stop { stop-color: var(--color-ink) }), so the pin is ink and nothing else. .sheet-pin is anchored with translate(-50%, -87%), which lands the drawing's entry line on the sheet's top edge: the head is pinned on the board, the entry on the paper. Decoration only — inside an aria-hidden="true" span with pointer-events: none — and the third of the document's owner-directed breaks (The Three Pinned Breaks); the facturitas' own alfiler (a real button) keeps the small inline PinIcon.

narrative.overview:
**Creative North Star: "La Factura del Mes"** — the month is a white invoice, bound like a
savings passbook, that the visitor keeps re-writing. The whole screen is one sheet of cool white
paper lying on a light honey wooden board — drawn, never photographed: its knots, plank joint and
grain are authored in CSS on the root element, with no raster and no external request. The
letterhead at the top, the month's three figures on one ruled band, and — under the small
perforation — the month's balance. Between the band and the cut sits the month itself as a **board
of facturitas**: one little invoice per record, grouped into ruled day blocks laid as a mosaic,
with the ones that matter pinned into a strip above. Nothing in it is a card: bands are separated
by rules, and the rules are the structure.

The sheet is written with the marks a person physically makes on a document. A rubber stamp
carries anything negative, anything over its cap, and the one action plate; a ballpoint carries
the original bolívar amount of a movement; a highlighter marks a cap that is running out — always
as a stroke behind the ink, never as a colour of its own. Attention that has to be legible as
text uses a darker amber instead. Income is not a colour at all: it is print ink at full strength
with a leading `+`, the way a signed page reads. Pinning is not a colour either: the alfiler is
an ink mark and a pressed state.

Every figure carries its provenance on the ticket beside it — the correlative `Nº`, the date, the
wallet and the note that produced it — so the visitor sees the month already closed into a total
and still knows where each part of it came from. The memorable moment is pinning: the alfiler
presses, the ticket lifts out of its day into the strip above, and the day block closes over the
gap it left. The two things this world refuses are named in its own material: the dashboard of
soft-shadowed KPI cards (there is one sheet, and nothing on it is elevated) and the bureaucratic
form (the movement form is a window over the sheet that first shows a "prueba de tira" — an
estimate of where the movement will land, labelled as an estimate, before anything is saved).
keyCharacteristics: One sheet on a light honey wooden board, ruled into bands; zero cards, and square corners belong to the paper (only the month's arrows and the perforation break it).
Cool white paper, near-black print ink; the only saturated fill is the stamp-red action plate.
Three marks only: stamp red, ballpoint blue, highlighter yellow — plus amber for attention text.
Libre Franklin for the document, Chivo Mono for every measured column, tabular figures everywhere.

Depth is material: one warm shadow for the sheet on the board, one for a window over the sheet, one for the action plate once it leaves the flow on a phone, and one drop-shadow that reads each torn facturita.

The sheet reads as pinned to the board: its own engraved ink thumbtack (`SheetPin.tsx`) sits over its top edge, and from `720px` up the whole sheet carries a `-0.3deg` tilt with its warm contact shadow retuned (The Three Pinned Breaks).
The board is drawn, never photographed — grain, plank joints and knots in CSS on the root element; no raster, no external request.
Both faces self-hosted and served from this origin; no external font, CDN or network request.
Two authored motions: the ink-dry re-print of the month's figures, and one flash on the facturita just written.

rules.name: The Three-Marks Rule
rules.body: Only three marks carry colour: the rubber stamp (red), the ballpoint (blue) and the highlighter (yellow). Amber is the same "attention" ink made readable as text. A fourth hue does not exist — a new state finds its mark, or it stays ink, and the alfiler is an ink mark and a pressed state, never a fourth colour.

rules.name: The Ink-Only-Income Rule
rules.body: Income is never a colour: `.fact-amt.income` is print ink at full strength with a leading `+`, exactly like `.fact-amt.expense`. The sign carries the meaning.

rules.name: The Highlighter-Behind-Ink Rule
rules.body: The highlighter is a background stroke, never a text colour. When attention must be legible as lettering it is amber (`.row.warn`, `.wbar.warn`) or it is ink.

rules.name: The Never-Grey Rule
rules.body: Secondary and tertiary text are ink at reduced alpha over paper (0.78 → 8.8:1, 0.66 → 5.7:1). No grey and no tinted neutral is ever used to lower the voice, because the sheet has to stay legible in daylight. Both neutrals were raised one step — `0.66` → `0.78` and `0.6` → `0.66` — when the invoice's secondary lines read washed out: at 0.66 and 0.6 the ticket's own lines were AA-passing but faint, and faint is what grey means here. Full ink stays `17.4:1`, so the hierarchy still reads; it is just no longer grey.

rules.name: The Authored-Board Rule
rules.body: The board is drawn, never photographed: a flat `--color-desk` ground carrying, top to bottom, its knots, a plank joint, three de-synchronised grain periods and one wide tonal band set — all CSS gradients on the root element, with no raster and no external request. It is authored at **two scales**, because the band it has to read in is not the same size on both screens. From `680px` up the side band is at least `60px`, and the wide set draws knots at x `1.5%`/`98.5%`, an `180px` plank joint, grain periods of `3px`/`7px`/`13px` and one horizontal tonal band set. At `679px` and below the band is only ~`18px` wide, and there the wide set's hairline grain (alpha `0.06` on a `3px` period) measured as a flat colour band, not as wood: the narrow set draws knots of ~`9px` (a dark ellipse at alpha `0.34` plus a light ring at `0.42`) at x `2%`/`97.5%`, a plank joint every `54px` so that both the left and the right band contain a plank edge, grain periods of `3px`/`5px`/`4px` at alphas `0.16`/`0.11`/`0.09`, and a `180°` tonal ramp that runs down the band instead of across it. Both sets are the same board drawn for the room it has, and that is the cost: two rule sets must be kept in step. It sits on the root element and not on a `.desk` wrapper, because the sheet's collapsed margins used to shrink that wrapper's box and leave flat, ungrained bands at the top and bottom of the document. And it only exists where it is visible: the knots sit at each scale's own x on purpose, so they land in the board's side band and are never hidden under the sheet.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` is declared on `body` and inherited by everything, and restated on `.mono`/`.num`. No column of figures may shift width.

rules.name: The Measured-Mono Rule
rules.body: Chivo Mono is for money, rates, dates, counts, correlative numbers and codes — things that are measured, matched or listed in a column. It is never used to make something look technical.

rules.name: The One-Line Section Rule
rules.body: A section opens with a `.sect`: one `0.74rem`/900/`0.16em` uppercase heading and its 1px ink rule sharing a baseline, with the optional `sect-note` in Ink Dim at the far end of the row. The heading carries its own weight; the rule supplies the division.

rules.name: The Counted-Day Rule
rules.body: A day block is headed by its day and the COUNT of its facturas, never by a money subtotal. PRODUCT.md makes the backend own every business figure and freezes the API, so the frontend may not sum: a day total waits for an API field.

rules.name: The Flat-Sheet Rule
rules.body: A surface never lifts. It is either printed on the sheet (fields, bars, tags, stamps, facturitas) or it is a window over it. A card with a soft shadow does not belong to this world. A facturita's drop-shadow does not lift it: it follows the torn silhouette and reads the cut, not height.

rules.name: The One-Shadow Rule
rules.body: A surface declares its depth once, as contact with what is under it: the sheet has one warm shadow on the board, the window has one over the sheet, the torn facturita has one on the paper beneath it, and the month's arrow chips have their one short paper shadow. Nothing else in the sheet casts anything — except the action plate, and only once it has left the flow to float over the sheet on a phone. The sheet's pin is not a second exception: its penumbra is an ink radial fill inside its own SVG (`.sheet-pin stop`), part of the drawing, not a shadow cast by a surface.

rules.name: The Three Pinned Breaks
rules.body: Three deliberate breaks of the old squareness are the user's, not drift. The month's `‹`/`›` arrows are `46px` paper **circles** (`border-radius: 50%`, `.mnav-btn`), and every facturita carries **one** `filter: drop-shadow` following its torn edge. The third is the sheet itself: it reads as a paper **pinned to the board**. The pin is now **its own engraved drawing** — `frontend/src/components/SheetPin.tsx`, mounted as `.sheet-pin` inside an `aria-hidden="true"` span with `pointer-events: none`, decoration only; the facturitas' own alfiler is a different thing and keeps the small inline `PinIcon`. It draws a head whose radial gradient runs from `0.4` to `1.0` of ink opacity — the same wide "engraved" opacity family the world's printed charts use, because a narrow range read as a flat black shape — an **unprinted highlight** on the dome (`.sheet-pin-gleam`, filled with `--color-paper`), the head's rim as a darker band, a collar and the needle's entry into the paper, over a **soft radial penumbra** for the cast shadow (it read as a flat base before). Its gradient stops take their colour from the token (`.sheet-pin stop { stop-color: var(--color-ink) }`), so the pin is ink and nothing else. `.sheet-pin` is anchored with `top: 0; left: 50%; transform: translate(-50%, -87%)`, which lands the drawing's entry line on the sheet's top edge: the head is pinned on the board, the entry on the paper. On `max-width: 719px` the same drawing renders smaller (`26×19.5px`), because the phone's board edge is only `18px` and the desktop size pushed the head off the top of the screen. And from `min-width: 720px` up the whole sheet carries a `rotate(-0.3deg)` tilt with its warm contact shadow retuned (`0 1px 0 rgba(58, 36, 10, 0.16), 0 13px 28px -17px rgba(58, 36, 10, 0.6)`) so it reads as lying pinned, not floating. The tilt is **desktop-only on purpose**: below `719px` the action plate is `position: fixed`, and a `transform` on `.sheet` would make that `fixed` resolve against the sheet and break the floating button — so on a phone the pin appears with no tilt. `.desk` carries `overflow-x: clip` so the tilt cannot cause horizontal overflow, and `@media print` hides the pin and drops the transform. One consequence belongs here because it comes from the same transform: because `.sheet` becomes the containing block for `fixed` descendants, the `.skip-link` was moved **out of** the sheet — it is now the first focusable element in the document, a sibling of `.desk` — so it keeps resolving against the viewport and still slides into the top-left corner. "Square corners everywhere" is now "square corners belong to the paper": the sheet, the facturita, the month's band and the lists stay square, and the `7px` perforation punch holes are no longer the only curve.

dos: Do keep one sheet and divide it with rules (`.sect`, `.rule`, 2px/3px closers, dashed tear lines). Bands are separated by ink, never by a card.

Do draw the board, never photograph it — grain, plank joints and knots as CSS gradients on the root element, no raster and no external request — keeping an `18px` cravat of board around the sheet below `680px` and at least `60px` of board on each side from `680px`; the phone's band is the same board at a smaller scale, and the two sets must be kept in step (The Authored-Board Rule).
Do measure every figure in Chivo Mono with tabular numerals (`.num`, `.mono`, `.pen`, `.cap`, `.fact-amt`) and push money to the right edge of its line.
Do set income as full ink with a leading `+`; the sign carries the meaning.
Do use the highlighter as a background stroke behind ink (`.mark`) and switch to amber (`--color-warn`, 4.8:1) the moment attention has to be lettering.
Do head a day block by its day and the COUNT of its facturas, never by a money subtotal (The Counted-Day Rule).
Do keep the stamp-red `.plate` the loudest element of the flow it belongs to.
Do keep the alfiler an ink mark and a pressed state, and swap only a pinned facturita's ground to Copy Paper.

Do cut a facturita's bottom edge with the authored `--tear` mask and give each ticket **one** `filter: drop-shadow` — a filter, not a `box-shadow`, because the mask clips it — since the tear is legible by that shadow alone, the paper resting on the sheet and not on the board (The Three Pinned Breaks).

Do put every interruption, form and destructive confirmation in the one window primitive with focus moved in, trapped and restored, Escape working, body scroll locked, and the panel positioned against the viewport so opening it never scrolls the document.
Do let every figure show its provenance: the correlative `Nº`, the date, the wallet and the note stay on the ticket beside the amount.

Do show a movement's detail lines on its facturita as a ruled breakdown — a `ul.fact-items` between the body and the actions, one `li` per line with the description left and its mono price right, opened by a 1px dashed `--color-rule` rule — in the movement's entry currency (bolívares for a VES movement, `formatBss`) and keep the total only in the header's `.fact-amt`, in USD; the backend derives the stored total from those lines — their sum, converted **once** for VES — and the client only ever shows an estimate.

Do give each jar's three figures their own labelled cells (`.jar-figs`: Objetivo / Gastado / Restante, label above a mono figure, a 1px `--color-rule` hairline between cells) with the status `.tag` on its own line above, and let them collapse to three ruled rows below `560px`, where three columns no longer fit a long amount.

Do read the sheet as pinned: its own engraved ink thumbtack (`.sheet-pin`, `SheetPin.tsx`) anchored so its entry line lands on the sheet's top edge — the same drawing redrawn at `26×19.5px` on a `719px` phone, where the board edge is only `18px` — and a `-0.3deg` tilt only from `720px` up with its warm contact shadow retuned; below `720px` the action plate floats fixed and the sheet stays straight (The Three Pinned Breaks).
Do label a client-side estimate as an estimate ("Estimado, todavía sin guardar") and never as the stored figure.

Do verify contrast as a number against the real ground (ink 0.78 → 8.8:1, ink 0.66 → 5.7:1, control 0.46 → 3.0:1, stamp on paper 6.1:1, paper on stamp fill 5.7:1), and size the controls for touch — fields and the plate 46px, page and icon buttons 42px, the alfiler and the ticket actions 34px, and a 44px floor on a coarse pointer — with one visible 2px focus ring.
Do keep both faces self-hosted and versioned in the document's own stylesheet: no CDN, no external font, no network request at runtime.
donts: Don't introduce a fourth hue or a coloured fill that is not the stamp plate. The only other full fill in the system is print ink (`.pbtn.primary`), which is not a colour — and the alfiler is not a colour at all.

Don't round a corner beyond the three pinned breaks: the sheet, the facturita, the month's band and the lists stay `border-radius: 0`, and the only curves are the `.perf` punch holes and the month's `46px` arrow circles.

Don't wrap a facturita in a card: it is a printed rectangle with a 1px Control Line border on a flat paper ground, torn along its bottom edge. Its one `filter: drop-shadow` reads the tear, not a lift — never a `box-shadow`, which the mask would clip.

Don't let a surface cast a shadow other than the sheet's warm ground shadow, a window's, the floating action plate's, a torn facturita's one drop-shadow or the month arrow chips'; a band's depth is its rule.
Don't use the highlighter yellow as a text colour, and don't colour an income.
Don't recompute a stored business figure in the client, and never sum a day: the API owns the numbers.
Don't lay the month out as rows behind table columns: a record is a facturita, a little printed rectangle, never a line in a table that a figure can hide behind.
Don't use `window.confirm`, a `role="alert"` per field, or a second live region.
Don't add an entrance animation per section: the only two motions in the system are the ink-dry re-print of the month's figures (240ms) and the single flash of the facturita just written.
